title: Drishyam: The Conclusion Trailer Drops September 9 Ahead of Gandhi Jayanti Release
excerpt: Ajay Devgn returns as Vijay Salgaonkar in the final chapter of Hindi cinema's most successful thriller franchise, with Jaideep Ahlawat and Prakash Raj joining the ensemble for an October 2 theatrical release.
body:
• The trailer for Drishyam: The Conclusion will be unveiled on September 9 at a star-studded launch event in Goa, ahead of the film's theatrical release on October 2 (Gandhi Jayanti)
  • The CBFC has cleared the 2-minute-52-second trailer with a U/A 16+ certificate, marking the first look at the franchise's concluding chapter
  • Jaideep Ahlawat and Prakash Raj join the franchise as Crime Branch SP Rajveer Singh Tomar and Lawyer Indrajith Shetty, respectively, raising the stakes against Vijay Salgaonkar
  • Director Abhishek Pathak says the story continues from where Drishyam 2 ended, with nearly two years spent developing the screenplay for the final chapter

The final chapter of Hindi cinema's most successful thriller franchise is about to get its first public airing. The makers of Drishyam: The Conclusion have announced that the film's theatrical trailer will be unveiled on September 9, setting up a month-long countdown to the October 2 release date — a date the studio has branded "Drishyam Day."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Y_aayoUh8gU

The Central Board of Film Certification cleared the trailer on September 1, granting it a U/A 16+ certificate. At 2 minutes and 52 seconds, the promo is expected to offer the first substantial look at the new threats facing the Salgaonkar family and the direction of the franchise's concluding installment.

The Salgaonkars, Back in the Crosshairs

Ajay Devgn returns as Vijay Salgaonkar, the ordinary family man whose extraordinary alibis have made him one of Hindi cinema's most iconic characters. Shriya Saran reprises her role as Nandini Salgaonkar, while Tabu returns as Meera Deshmukh — a character whose pursuit of justice now takes a deeply personal turn as she seeks revenge for the loss of her son.

https://x.com/Box_Office_BO/status/2096268706309619800

The announcement was accompanied by a new poster featuring the cast, with the tagline: "Iss baar khatra aur bhi bada hai. Salgaonkar parivaar... wapas ghere mein hai" (This time the danger is even greater. The Salgaonkar family is under siege again).

New Faces Raise the Stakes

The franchise has expanded its ensemble with two significant additions. Jaideep Ahlawat, best known for his work in Paatal Lok, enters the Drishyam universe as Rajveer Singh Tomar, an SP in the Crime Branch, bringing a formidable new investigative threat. Prakash Raj joins as Lawyer Indrajith Shetty, adding legal and tactical pressure on the Salgaonkar family from a different angle.

"After Drishyam 2, it took us almost a year to crack the story and another year to develop and write the screenplay. The story continues from where the second film ended but the journey ahead is completely new."

— Abhishek Pathak, Director

Rajat Kapoor returns as Mahesh Deshmukh, a father still carrying the weight of his son's disappearance, while Kamlesh Sawant, Ishita Dutta, and Mrunal Jadhav complete the returning cast.

Goa Launch Mirrors Drishyam 2 Playbook

The trailer launch is planned as a high-profile event in Goa, with the entire star cast expected to attend. The choice of venue mirrors the promotional strategy used for Drishyam 2 in 2022, which also held its trailer launch in the coastal state — a nod to the franchise's Goan setting.

Presented by Star Studio18 and produced under the Panorama Studios banner, Drishyam: The Conclusion is directed by Abhishek Pathak, who helmed the previous Hindi chapter. He co-wrote the screenplay with Aamil Keeyan Khan and Parveez Shaikh, with Alok Jain, Ajit Andhare, Kumar Mangat Pathak, and Abhishek Pathak serving as producers.

The Drishyam franchise, originally a Malayalam film by Jeethu Joseph starring Mohanlal, has been remade in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and Kannada. The Malayalam Drishyam 3 released theatrically earlier this year and crossed ₹231 crore at the box office before streaming on Prime Video in June. The Hindi version has charted its own course, with Drishyam 2 (2022) becoming one of Bollywood's biggest post-pandemic hits.

For diaspora audiences who have followed Vijay Salgaonkar's story across both language versions, the question that has sustained the franchise through three films remains the same: does he finally get caught, or does he outsmart the system one last time? The September 9 trailer should begin to answer that.
nri_angle: The Drishyam franchise is hugely popular among Indian diaspora audiences in the US, who have followed both the Malayalam and Hindi versions of Vijay Salgaonkar's story.
